extracted.intended_audience: Members of Congress, legislative staff, USPTO policymakers, patent practitioners, and stakeholders (small businesses and inventors)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and summarize statutory amendment provisions and policy criteria debated on the House floor relating to the America Invents Act (AIA), addressing diversity studies, satellite offices, small-business supports, international patent assistance, tax-strategy patents, and takings concerns. Useful for legislative analysts, patent counsel, and stakeholder advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of methods for studying the diversity of applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall, not later than the end of the 6-month period beginning on the date of enactment, establish methods for studying the diversity of patent applicants, including those applicants who are minorities, women, or veterans. The Director shall not use the results of such study to provide any preferential treatment to patent applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: obtain proper data to identify under-participating sectors and guide outreach. Rationale provided: current PTO data is limited (name and general location only, often attorney address), preventing understanding of underrepresentation; examples and survey evidence (Kauffman, NSF) cited. Explicit prohibition on using study results for preferential treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of Congress on patent system goals
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the sense of Congress that the patent system should promote industries to continue to develop new technologies that spur growth and create jobs across the country, which includes protecting the rights of small businesses and inventors from predatory behavior that could result in the cutting off of innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing principle intended to guide interpretation and implementation: emphasize innovation, job creation, and protection of small businesses from predatory entities (e.g., 'patent trolls'). Used to argue for provisions that consider small-entity impacts and guard against measures that would chill innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for selection of USPTO satellite office locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall evaluate and consider: (C) the extent to which the purposes of satellite offices will be achieved; (D) the availability of scientific and technically knowledgeable personnel in the region from which to draw new patent examiners at minimal recruitment cost; and (E) the economic impact to the region. Selection must include an explanation of how the selected location will achieve the purposes and how the required considerations were met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: ensure satellite offices increase outreach and access for small businesses/independent inventors, reduce recruitment costs (save taxpayers), and support regional economic growth. Rationale: current bill lists purposes but did not make them part of the selection process; amendment makes those purposes explicit selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO study on international patent protections for small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director, in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration, shall, using existing resources of the Office, carry out a study to determine how the Office, in coordination with other Federal departments and agencies, can best help small businesses with international patent protection; and whether there should be established either (A) a revolving fund loan program to make loans to small businesses to defray costs of filing, maintaining, and enforcing international patent applications and related technical assistance, or (B) a grant program to defray such costs and assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report required within 120 days containing findings, a statement whether either program should be established (loan, grant, or neither), and any legislative recommendations. Sponsors emphasize study should use existing resources and be no-cost; opponents warn against creating new entitlement programs or taxpayer-funded payments to foreign governments. Suggested focus: outreach, education, and technical assistance rather than direct funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of tax strategy patents and retroactivity concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: H.R. 1249 deems tax strategies insufficient to differentiate a claimed invention from the prior art (effectively banning tax strategy patents). Debate: an amendment would prevent retroactive nullification of pending tax-strategy patent applications (protecting applicants who filed in reliance on prior law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy tension: eliminate tax-strategy patents prospectively to avoid burdening taxpayers, while addressing fairness for applicants who disclosed innovations under earlier rules. Arguments: published/pending applications disclosure means applicants lose trade-secret value if patents are retroactively disallowed; retroactivity raises takings/equity concerns. Sponsors argue ban prevents additional complexity and costs to taxpayers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for small entities relating to transitional review program (takings concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns were raised that Section 18 (transitional review program for business-method patents) could create conditions running afoul of the Takings Clause. Proposed protective measures included shortening the sunset on Section 18 from 10 years to 5 years and requiring the Director to make a determination of whether a condition causing an unlawful taking is created by the section; additionally, a proposed sense of Congress that no provisions should create an unconstitutional taking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: protect small businesses from potential devaluation or uncompensated government action. Sponsors sought either procedural safeguards (Director determination) or substantive limits (shorter sunset) to reduce constitutional risk. Framing: protect property rights while implementing review mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of minority and women-owned businesses in small-entity definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments to ensure the inclusion of minority and women-owned businesses in the definition of 'small entities' so they receive the benefits of reduced user fees and similar small-entity advantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: ensure fee discounts and small-entity supports reach historically underrepresented owners and institutions (e.g., HBCUs, Hispanic-Serving Institutions). Presented as a pro-small-business amendment to promote equity in access to patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of grace period for small businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendment to extend the grace period for small businesses from one year to 18 months to enable them enough time to secure financial support and develop their invention prior to losing grace protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: longer grace helps small entities obtain investors and develop inventions without losing patentability; positioned as a transitional/ small-business protective measure to reduce risk when seeking funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business outreach, ombudsman, and education as tools to help protect IP
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill includes creating a permanent small business ombudsman at the PTO and directs the PTO to conduct small business outreach programs throughout the country to teach small businesses about IP enforcement and how to protect their intellectual property domestically and abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors and supporters emphasize that outreach, education, and technical assistance are effective, low-cost tools (preferred over new funding programs) to help small businesses obtain and enforce patent protections. Opponents of subsidy-style proposals point to these existing programs as alternatives to taxpayer-funded loan/grant schemes.
